sources.title: Using trauma-informed language
sources.quote: Validate the person’s experience without judgement – don’t rush to express concern, offer advice or solutions.
sources.technique: Acknowledge and validate the person’s experience without judgement, and do not offer advice or solutions before they feel heard; offer options collaboratively.

sources.title: Motivational Interviewing: Steps and Core Skills
sources.quote: The four steps of the MI process are engage, focus, evoke, and plan.
sources.technique: Engage with empathy and open questions, focus on understanding what the person says and feels, and evoke their concerns before moving to planning.

sources.title: Informing and advising as core skill of MI
sources.quote: Offering information or advice with permission.
sources.technique: Before giving advice, ask permission and clarify what information the person wants; after sharing it, invite their interpretation and response.

sources.title: Associated Document: Validating and Invalidating Statements and Curious Questions (Adapted from: www.borderlinepersonalitydisorder.com)
sources.quote: Remember not to focus on what happened; focus on how the patient feels about the situation.
sources.technique: Respond to the person’s feelings with emotional language, reflect what you hear, and ask curious questions rather than jumping to advice.
